name: Battle of Manzikert

phases.title: The Byzantines form up and march out
phases.text: The Byzantine army gathered into battle formation and marched on the Seljuk positions, with Bryennios on the left, Theodore Alyates on the right and the emperor in the centre. Andronikos Doukas held the reserve in the rear, and the Seljuks stood in a crescent about four kilometres away.

phases.title: Horse archers draw the crescent round them
phases.text: Seljuk horse archers shot at the Byzantines as they drew closer. The centre of the crescent kept falling back while the wings moved round to surround the advancing troops.

phases.title: The Byzantines take the camp, but the wings fray
phases.text: The Byzantine centre pressed on despite the arrows and captured Alp Arslan's camp by the end of the afternoon. The wings, where the arrows did most damage, almost broke up as units tried to force a pitched battle, and the Seljuk cavalry simply disengaged when challenged.

phases.title: The withdrawal is ordered and misunderstood
phases.text: With the Seljuks avoiding battle, Romanos ordered a withdrawal. The right wing misunderstood the order, and Doukas ignored it and marched his reserve straight back to the camp outside Manzikert instead of covering the retreat.

phases.title: The Seljuks attack and the right wing breaks
phases.text: With the Byzantines confused, the Seljuks attacked. The right wing was almost at once routed, its men thinking they had been betrayed.

phases.title: The left wing is routed and the centre encircled
phases.text: The left wing under Bryennios held out a little longer but was soon routed. The Seljuks encircled what remained of the centre, including the emperor and the Varangian Guard, and Romanos was wounded and taken prisoner.

note: The accounts do not give compass directions, so the Byzantines are drawn on the left and the Seljuks on the right. The hills where the Seljuks had hidden the night before are placed behind their line, and the two camps are placed by judgement; the accounts do not say exactly where they lay. The Seljuk wings are drawn as an upper and a lower horn of the crescent. The accounts differ on whether the Armenians fled first or stood to the end.
